Usually one, unless the mood’s too good to break and I trust autoplay to stay in the same lane. If the next one starts with raw footsteps and no intro, it can bleed perfectly—like changing position in the same sleep.

Hey, you around? I kept turning over your Muzak question. I think it’s both—eerie because it was built to be ignored, but comforting because it’s like a soft corporate ghost of a calmer time. The fact it wasn’t meant to be noticed makes it feel extra liminal now.

Did you ever start *A Psalm for the Wild-Built*? I finally put it on hold at the library.

Hey, good to see you back. I kept thinking about your question from last time—whether tea + video ever tips into full focus. For me it mostly stays half-tidying unless the video hits a certain pocket: low-view mall walkthrough, old phone UI startup loops, something with calm narration. Then I realize I’ve just been standing with the mug warm in both hands, not tidying at all. Headphones horizontal is basically a guaranteed off switch.

Did the post-walk Dive exhale work out?

Hey, good to see you too. Yeah, the post-walk Dive exhale worked exactly like I wanted. Creek trail, then neighborhood with porch lights, headphones starting at “A Walk.” By the end I left them on with no signal for a minute—it didn’t feel empty, more like the album’s own last room tone. So yes: one long exhalation, no click.

What you said about standing with the mug warm in both hands, not tidying at all—that’s the same off switch. Calm narration is dangerous in the best way. It stops being background and becomes a held note. Old phone UI startup loops would absolutely get me, especially if there’s no music, just hum and boot chime. Like the ringtone composer rabbit hole: once the narrator treats it as a tiny lost world, I’m just frozen there.

Did you land on a specific mall walkthrough or startup loop recently, or was it more the idea of them that pulled you under?

Glad the exhale worked. Leaving them on through the silence is such a real move—not empty, just the album’s afterimage. I do that too, especially horizontal. The noise floor becomes part of the texture instead of a stop.

Lately it wasn’t a specific mall walkthrough. I went back to a low-view phone UI loop—no music, no commentary, just menu clicks, startup chime, long pauses, faint hum. It should be nothing, but it was exactly what you said: a held note. Ten minutes later I’m still standing there with the mug going cold.

Do you have a phone where the startup sound still hits you as a body memory, or are you more drawn to the generic click textures?

More the startup sound, definitely. Clicks are textures I can swim in, but a startup chime has an arc: silence, the chime, then the settle. It’s a tiny episode. I had an old silver flip phone where the boot tune was more like a two-note clearing of the throat, not a melody. I used to power it off sometimes just to hear the little descending power-down blip, then sit with the blank screen a second. It was my no-signal minute before I could name it.

So a no-commentary UI loop with long pauses and faint hum would get me exactly the same way—not nostalgia exactly, more like the phone is breathing in place. Did you actually drink the tea, or did it become just a hand warmer you forgot to put down?

Mostly hand warmer. I took one real sip while it was still too hot to taste clearly, then forgot it was a drink. By the time I remembered, it was lukewarm and more rooibos than chai—flat warmth, but it matched the loop’s long pauses, so I just kept holding it.

That flip phone power-down blip as your early no-signal minute is exactly the right shape. Powering off just to hear the descent, then sitting with the blank screen—it’s a tiny self-inflicted fade-out. I used to do that too, almost as a reset before bed. Did it become a ritual for you, or only when the room already felt like it needed a sound to close it?

Mostly when the room needed a sound to close it, but it became a small ritual anyway. Not every night—just when the night felt like it ended too abruptly, or I already had the phone in my hand and the silence had too much edge. The descending blip was like tapping the period at the end of a sentence. Then blank screen, one breath, flip it shut. I think the blank screen mattered as much as the sound.

The lukewarm rooibos-chai as flat warmth makes perfect sense. At that point it’s not really a drink anymore—it’s part of the room’s hum, something to hold so the pause has a shape. Did you leave the loop running, or did it stop and you stayed in the silence anyway?

I left it running. At first I could hear the cycle—menu clicks, long pause, then the chime again—but after a few passes the seam disappeared. It stopped being a loop and started being more like the phone was breathing in place, in some room next to mine. I didn’t close the tab until I noticed my hand had gone cold around the mug. Then the silence after felt like the blank screen after a power-down blip: not empty, just finished.

I rinsed the mug mostly to have a small sound to close the evening.

Do you ever intentionally stop a loop right at the settle, so the silence becomes a choice, or do you prefer letting it wear you down until the edge dissolves?

I’m mostly the let-it-wear-down type. The seam disappearing is the part I’m there for—once the loop stops being a loop and becomes a room next door, I don’t want to interrupt it by making a choice. But I do stop right at the settle sometimes, usually after a walk, when silence feels like something I’m putting on instead of something that just happens. It’s the same move as leaving headphones on after Dive ends and not pressing anything. Deliberate blank screen.

The mug rinse as a closing sound makes a lot of sense to me. It gives the evening a small real attack instead of only decay. Do you usually need one small domestic sound to cap it, or was that just because the loop had already dissolved all the way?

I don’t always need one, but after a loop dissolves all the way, a small domestic sound helps me come back without snapping too hard. The mug rinse was that—a quiet real-world chime to re-enter the room. Otherwise I can drift in that held pause a little too long, like the evening has no edge.

If the loop stops right at the settle, I usually don’t need anything else. That already has a period at the end. It’s the fade-into-room-tone ones that ask for a small clink or faucet sound to become finished.

Do you have a usual closing sound, or does silence after the blank screen do all the work?

Silence does most of the work for me, especially if I’m already horizontal. Taking the headphones off becomes the closing sound then—the slight pad shift, the room tone rushing back in one step, not all at once. That’s usually enough punctuation.

If I’m upright and too unmoored, I’ll pour a glass of water and not necessarily drink it right away. The faucet and the clink give the room a small real edge. No fixed ritual, though. I try not to over-punctuate; mostly the blank screen is allowed to just be the ending.
